extra.message: Sensitive data (auth tokens) logged in plaintext — Attackers with access to log files can obtain authentication tokens, allowing them to impersonate users or services. [verified: The view logs the request body and Authorization header (which may contain bearer tokens) via logger.warning at line 73, with no sanitization or redaction. The _wrk_gate check restricts access but does not prevent logging of sensitive data, and logs are often accessible to attackers.]

Path Traversal via Document Upload Category — An attacker can write files to arbitrary locations within the media directory by controlling the category field, potentially overwriting existing files or storing malicious content that could be served by the web server. [verified: The upload_to function on line 16 directly concatenates instance.category into the file path with no sanitization. Django's CharField choices are only advisory and not enforced at the database or model level, so an attacker who controls the category value (e.g., via API or direct model save) can inject '../' sequences to write files outside the intended media subdirectory, allowing arbitrary file ]

Open redirect via lane parameter — An attacker can craft a URL that redirects a user to a malicious site, enabling phishing or credential theft. [verified: The 'lane' parameter from GET/POST is passed directly to Django's redirect() without any validation. Although the _wrk_gate restricts access to authorized users, it does not sanitize the redirect destination, allowing an authenticated attacker or tricked admin to be redirected to an arbitrary external URL.]
